record.title: The uniform sets bounded-sums conjecture
record.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ and $k\geq2$. Let $\Phi=(\Phi_N)_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a Følner sequence. A set is $\mathsf{U}^k(\Phi)$-uniform when its indicator has correlations along $\Phi$, positive density along $\Phi$, and vanishing $\mathsf{U}^k(\Phi)$ seminorm after subtracting its density. For an infinite $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ and $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$, write

$$
B^{\oplus\ell}=\left\{\sum_{n\in F}n:F\subset B,\ |F|=\ell\right\}.
$$

**Uniform sets bounded-sums conjecture.** If $A$ is $\mathsf{U}^k(\Phi)$-uniform for some Følner sequence $\Phi$, then for every $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\in\mathbb{N}$ there is an infinite set $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
B^{\oplus\ell_1},B^{\oplus\ell_2},\ldots,B^{\oplus\ell_k}\subset A.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the relevant uniformity hypotheses remove the shift required in the general positive-density problem. It is stated without a resolution in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Bryna Kra, Joel Moreira, Florian K. Richter and Donald Robertson, “Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond”, arXiv:2311.06197 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.06197

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2023). “The case $k=2$ of , which corresponds to a slight variation of , is proved in .”

record.title: Polynomial-time precoloring extension for bounded outer faces
record.statement:
A **planar near-Eulerian-triangulation** is a planar graph in which every bounded face is a triangle and every vertex has even degree; a **precoloring** assigns colors from a set of four colors to the vertices incident with the outer face. For a positive integer $\ell$, consider instances whose outer face has length at most $\ell$.

**Polynomial-time precoloring-extension conjecture.** For every positive integer $\ell$, there is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a planar near-Eulerian-triangulation $G$ with outer face of length at most $\ell$ and a precoloring $\varphi$ of the vertices incident with the outer face, decides whether $\varphi$ extends to a 4-coloring of $G$.

This conjecture extends the proved linear-time result for outer faces of length at most five and would resolve the disk case for every fixed boundary length. The source gives no resolution beyond these bounded-length results.
record.source_name: Zdeněk Dvořák, Benjamin Moore, Michaela Seifrtová and Robert Šámal, “Precoloring extension in planar near-Eulerian-triangulations”, arXiv:2312.13061 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13061

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2023).

record.title: Tournament Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture for forest backedge graphs
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tournament with an ordering of its vertices, and let the corresponding backedge graph be the graph whose edges are the arcs directed backwards in that ordering. A tournament class is **dichromatically bounded by clique number** if there is a function $f$ such that every tournament in the class satisfies

$$
\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\chi}}(T)\leq f(\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\omega}}(T)).
$$

**Tournament Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture.** If $T$ has a backedge graph that is a forest, then the class of tournaments not containing $T$ as a subgraph is dichromatically bounded by clique number. The source states this as an analogue of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture and does not give a resolution here.
record.source_name: Guillaume Aubian, “Computing the clique number of tournaments”, arXiv:2401.07776 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.07776

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2024). “This question was answered in the negative by Zykov in .”

record.title: Kuratowski-type coarse planarisation conjecture
record.statement:
A graph has a **$K$-fat $K_5$ and $K_{3,3}$ minor** if it contains both $K_5$ and $K_{3,3}$ as fat minors with parameter $K$. Let

$$
f \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}.
$$

**Kuratowski-type coarse planarisation conjecture.** There exists a function $f$ such that every graph with no $K$-fat $K_5$ and $K_{3,3}$ minor is $f(K)$-quasi-isometric to a planar graph.

This is described as a coarse variant of Kuratowski's theorem and as a special case of the broader Georgakopoulos–Papasoglu conjecture. The paper states that this special case remains open.
record.source_name: Sandra Albrechtsen, Raphael W. Jacobs, Paul Knappe and Paul Wollan, “A characterisation of graphs quasi-isometric to K_4-minor-free graphs”, arXiv:2408.15335 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15335

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2024). “Recently, has been disproved by Davies, Hickingbotham, Illingworth and McCarty for general graphs $X$ *{Theorem 1}.”

record.title: The general Ramsey–Turán formula conjecture for \(\rho(3,q)\)
record.statement:
For each integer $q\ge 5$, let $\rho(3,m)$ denote the Ramsey–Turán density for graphs admitting a 2-edge-coloring with no monochromatic blue $K_3$ and no monochromatic red $K_m$, and let $r(3,q)$ denote the classical Ramsey number. **The general Ramsey–Turán formula conjecture.** 
$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \rho(3,2q-1)=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{r(3,q)-1}\right), &\\ \rho(3,2q)=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{r(3,q)}\right). & \end{array} \right.
$$
 This statement appears in an ignored concluding passage and is presented as a conjecture about the wide-open values of $\rho(3,q)$ for $q\ge 8$; its resolution is not supplied, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Xinyu Hu and Qizhong Lin, “A step towards the Ramsey-Turán conjecture for K_3 and K_6”, arXiv:2409.04042 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.04042

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

record.title: Rafla's conjecture on crossing-free Hamiltonian cycles in simple drawings
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph, and let a **simple drawing** be a drawing in which any two edges have at most one common point and no two edges incident to the same vertex cross. A **crossing-free Hamiltonian cycle** is a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once and whose edges do not cross. **Rafla's conjecture.** Every simple drawing of $K_n$ with $n \geq 3$ vertices contains a crossing-free Hamiltonian cycle.

This conjecture asks whether the familiar property of straight-line drawings of complete graphs extends to all simple drawings. It was conjectured by Rafla in 1988; the supplied text gives no evidence of a general resolution, although it records proofs for several restricted drawing classes.
record.source_name: Oswin Aichholzer, Joachim Orthaber and Birgit Vogtenhuber, “Separable Drawings: Extendability and Crossing-Free Hamiltonian Cycles”, arXiv:2410.09922 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09922

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

record.title: Conlon–Fox–Gunby–He–Mubayi–Suk–Verstraëte–Yu conjecture for generalized Erdős–Rogers numbers
record.statement:
Let a **3-graph** be a 3-uniform hypergraph, let $K^3_3$ denote the complete 3-graph on three vertices, and let an $F$-iterated blowup denote the hypergraph construction obtained by repeatedly replacing vertices according to $F$. For a 3-graph $G$, let $f_{K^3_3,G}(n)$ be the corresponding generalized Erdős–Rogers number.

**Conlon–Fox–Gunby–He–Mubayi–Suk–Verstraëte–Yu conjecture.** There exists a constant $c=c(G)$ such that

$$
f_{K^3_3,G}(n)\ge n^c
$$

if and only if $G$ is a subgraph of a $K^3_3$-iterated blowup.

This conjecture characterizes precisely when the generalized Erdős–Rogers number for the triangle hypergraph has a polynomial lower bound; its resolution is not supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Xiaoyu He and Jiaxi Nie, “Generalized Erdős-Rogers problems for hypergraphs”, arXiv:2504.03138 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.03138

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

record.title: The $K_7^{=}$-minor 6-colorability conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K_7^{=}$ be the graph obtained from the complete graph $K_7$ by deleting two edges. A graph is **$K_7^{=}$-minor-free** if it has no minor isomorphic to $K_7^{=}$.

**$K_7^{=}$-minor 6-colorability conjecture.** Every graph with no $K_7^{=}$-minor is $6$-colorable.

This is proposed as the symmetrical counterpart to the paper's proved result for $K_7^{\vee}$, where the two deleted edges have a common end. The conjecture is presented as open, and the source notes that an appropriate extremal theorem is still missing.
record.source_name: Sergey Norin and Agnes Totschnig, “Every graph with no K_7^-minor is 6-colorable”, arXiv:2507.03244 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03244

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).

record.title: Seymour's improvement conjecture for Hadwiger numbers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number, and let $\operatorname{had}(G)$ denote its Hadwiger number. **Seymour's improvement conjecture.** There is a constant $\varepsilon > 0$ such that every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G) \leqslant 2$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{had}(G) \geqslant \left(\frac{1}{3} + \varepsilon\right)|V(G)|.
$$

This would improve the classical $|V(G)|/3$ lower bound for graphs with independence number $2$ and is presented as an open conjecture related to Hadwiger's conjecture.
record.source_name: Jung Hon Yip, “Dense Matchings of Linear Size in Graphs with Independence Number 2”, arXiv:2512.01401 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01401

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: Reduced TAS-tree conjecture for trees without isomorphic pairs
record.statement:
An **undirected tree** is a connected graph with no cycles. A **caterpillar** is a tree for which removing all leaves results in a path. An **isomorphic pair** in a graph consists of disjoint vertex sets inducing isomorphic subgraphs and satisfying the specified two-edge cut condition. An orientation has the **tournament anti-Sidorenko property** (TAS) when it satisfies the tournament anti-Sidorenko inequality.

**Reduced TAS-tree conjecture.** For every undirected tree that is not a caterpillar, has at least $2$ vertices of even degree, and has no isomorphic pair, there exists some orientation that has the tournament anti-Sidorenko property.

Caterpillars and trees reducible by isomorphic-pair pruning are already covered by results in the paper, so this conjecture is the remaining reduced case of the TAS-tree problem.
record.source_name: Xiaoyu He, Nitya Mani, Jiaxi Nie, Nathan Tung and Fan Wei, “New Sidorenko-type inequalities in tournaments”, arXiv:2512.11222 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.11222

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2025). “A small tree for which Conjecture remains open is the $2-3-4$ tree.”

record.title: Seymour's epsilon conjecture for graphs with independence number two
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $\operatorname{had}(G)$ be its Hadwiger number. **Seymour's epsilon conjecture.** There is a constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)=2$ satisfies 
$$
\operatorname{had}(G)\geqslant\left(\frac13+\varepsilon\right)|V(G)|.
$$
 This conjecture asks for any improvement over the classical $|V(G)|/3$ lower bound and is presented as an open problem.
record.source_name: Jofre Costa, Eric Luu, David R. Wood and Jung Hon Yip, “Verifying Hadwiger's Conjecture for Examples of Graphs with α(G) = 2”, arXiv:2512.17114 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17114

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: Erdős–Faudree conjecture on Hamiltonian subsets of regular Dirac graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be an $(n+1)$-regular graph on $2n$ vertices. A subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ is called Hamiltonian when the induced subgraph $G[S]$ contains a Hamilton cycle. **Erdős–Faudree conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that $G$ has at least $c2^{2n}$ Hamiltonian subsets. The source presents this as a question of Erdős and Faudree; no resolution is supplied in the given text.
record.source_name: Wanting Sun, Shunan Wei and Donglei Yang, “Clique factors in random samplings of regular graphs”, arXiv:2512.20287 (2025).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2503.01826](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01826).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20287

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2025). “This conjecture was resolved by Cuckler and Kahn . {We refer the reader to a survey of Sudakov where various measures of robustness and relevant results are collected.”

record.title: Generic bipartite reconstruction by low-order type constraints
record.statement: Let $G=(U,V,E)$ be a bipartite graph with $|U|=u$ and $|V|=v$, and let $\mathcal{D}(G)$ denote its vertex-deletion deck. Assume that $G$ is 2-connected, not regular, and has minimum degree at least $6$. For each vertex define its type by $\tau=(\deg,P)$, where $P$ is its neighbor-degree profile, and let $R(\cdot,\cdot)$ denote the resulting type-count constraints. **Generic bipartite reconstruction conjecture.** For generic such $G$, the deck determines $G$ uniquely up to bipartite isomorphism, and $G$ can be reconstructed in polynomial time by recovering degrees and profiles, imposing the type-count constraints, and selecting the unique feasible adjacency using two-deletion compatibility. This is an experimentally motivated claim restricted to a generic, moderately dense regime; neither the genericity condition nor the asserted polynomial-time reconstruction is established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Gergely Bérczi, “Evolving Local Corrections for Global Constructions in Combinatorics”, arXiv:2603.06692 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06692

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026). “Rota formulated this conjecture in the late 1980s, and it has since become a central open problem in matroid theory.”

record.title: Erdős–Kleitman matching conjecture for set families
record.statement:
Let $e(n,s)$ denote the maximum size of a family $\mathcal{F}\subset 2^{[n]}$ with matching number $\nu(\mathcal{F})<s$. For $1\leq i\leq k$, let

$$
\mathcal{A}_i^{(k)}(n,s)=\Bigl\{F\in {[n]\choose k}:|F\cap [si-1]|\ge i\Bigr\}.
$$

Let $\mathcal{P}(m,s,\ell)$ be the family defined for $n=sm+s-\ell$ by

$$
\mathcal{P}(m,s,\ell)=\bigl\{P\subset [n]: |P|+|P\cap [\ell-1]|\ge m+1\bigr\}.
$$

**Erdős–Kleitman matching conjecture.** Suppose that $s\ge 2$, $m\ge 1$, and $n=sm+s-\ell$ for some integer $0<\ell\leq\lceil s/2\rceil$. Then

$$
e(sm+s-\ell,s)=|\mathcal{P}(m,s,\ell)|.
$$

The conjecture concerns the extremal size of set families avoiding an $s$-matching. It is known in several cases, including $\ell=2$, $m=1$, $s\geq \ell m+3\ell+3$, and $m=2$, while the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Andrey Kupavskii and Georgy Sokolov, “More on the Erdős–Kleitman problem on matchings in set families”, arXiv:2605.04379 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04379

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2026).

record.title: Polynomial bound for tree-independence number in star-free induced-grid-minor-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 2$ be an integer, let $G$ be a $K_{1,d}$-free graph, and let $f$ be a polynomial. **Polynomial-bound conjecture.** There is a polynomial $f$ such that, whenever $G$ does not contain a $d\times d$ grid as an induced minor, its tree-independence number satisfies

$$
\alpha\text{-}\mathsf{tw}(G)\leq f(d).
$$

The question strengthens the induced-grid characterization by asking for a polynomial bound in $d$; the paper states it as an open problem and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Kenny Bešter Štorgel, Mujin Choi, Hidde Koerts and Ðorđe Vasić, “Tree-independence number of K_1,d-free graph classes”, arXiv:2606.20256 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20256

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

record.title: Erdős–Pósa-type conjecture for cycles of distinct lengths
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $\Lambda(G)=\{\ell\in\mathbb{N}\mid G\text{ contains a cycle of length }\ell\}$, and let $G-X$ denote the graph obtained by deleting the vertices in $X$. **Distinct-length cycle packing-cover conjecture.** There exists a function $f(k)\in\mathcal{O}(k\log k)$ such that every graph $G$ contains $k$ vertex-disjoint cycles with distinct lengths, or a set $X$ of at most $f(k)$ vertices such that

$$
|\Lambda(G-X)|\leq k-1.
$$

This proposes an Erdős–Pósa-type dual certificate for cycles of pairwise distinct lengths; the source presents it as a possible improvement and does not state that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: J. Pascal Gollin, Maximilian Gorsky, Meike Hatzel, Kevin Hendrey, Tony Huynh, Caleb McFarland, Marek Sokołowski, Sebastian Wiederrecht and Paul Wollan, “An Erdős-Pósa theorem for cycles and faces of distinct lengths”, arXiv:2607.06869 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06869

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2026). “That is, we leave the following as an open problem.”

record.title: Jackson–Thomassen conjecture on strong orientations of digraphs
record.statement:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph. It is **$k$-strong** if it has at least $k+1$ vertices and remains strongly connected after the deletion of any subset of $k-1$ vertices. An **oriented subdigraph** is obtained by retaining exactly one arc from every directed $2$-cycle of $D$.

**Jackson–Thomassen conjecture.** Every $2k$-strong digraph has a spanning $k$-strong oriented subdigraph.

For $k=1$, this follows from a result of Boesch and Tindell on strong orientations of mixed graphs, and the conjecture is known for symmetric digraphs by Thomassen. It remains open even for $k=2$ in general.
record.source_name: Tong Zhou, Jørgen Bang-Jensen, Jia Zhou and Jin Yan, “K-Arc-Strong Orientations Of Semicomplete Digraphs”, arXiv:2607.17116 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17116

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2026). “For $k=1$ this follows from a result of Boesch and Tindell on strong orientations of mixed graphs but the conjecture is open even for $k=2$, except for symmetric digraphs where Thomassen proved the conjecture .”

record.title: The strong Seymour vertex conjecture for oriented graphs
record.statement: Let $D$ be an oriented graph. For a vertex $x$, let $N_D^+(x)$ and $N_D^{++}(x)$ denote its out-neighborhood and second out-neighborhood, respectively. A **complete matching** from $X$ to $Y$ is a matching consisting of arcs directed from vertices of $X$ to vertices of $Y$ and having every vertex of $X$ as a tail. A vertex $x$ is a **strong Seymour vertex** if there is a complete matching from $N_D^+(x)$ to $N_D^{++}(x)$. **Strong Seymour vertex conjecture.** Every oriented graph contains a strong Seymour vertex. This would strengthen Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture, since a complete matching injects $N_D^+(x)$ into $N_D^{++}(x)$. It is proved in the paper for oriented graphs with minimum out-degree at most $5$ and for $5$-anti-transitive oriented graphs, and hence for oriented planar graphs; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Yandong Bai, Binlong Li and Boram Park, “Towards a strengthening of the second neighborhood conjecture”, arXiv:2607.18047 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18047

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

record.title: Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp cycle-versus-clique Ramsey conjecture
record.statement:
For graphs $G$ and $H$, let $R(G,H)$ denote the least integer $N$ such that every red-blue colouring of the edges of $K_N$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$. **Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture.** If $n\geq m\geq 3$, then 
$$
R(C_n,K_m)=(n-1)(m-1)+1.
$$
 The source says this remains open, although it is known in several broad parameter ranges.
record.source_name: Richard Montgomery, “Recent progress in graph theory using expansion”, arXiv:2607.26049 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26049

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

record.title: Linear Erdős–Pósa bound for models of forests
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a forest and let $R \subseteq V(F)$. For a graph $G$, a set $S \subseteq V(G)$, and a positive integer $k$, consider models of $(F,R)$ in $(G,S)$.

**Linear Erdős–Pósa conjecture.** At least one of the following holds:

1. There are $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint models of $(F,R)$ in $(G,S)$.
2. There is a set $X \subseteq V(G)$ with

$$
|X| \leq |V(F)|(k-1)
$$

such that there is no model of $(F,R)$ in $(G-X,S \setminus X)$.

This would give a bound linear in the size of the forest, improving the dependence on $|V(T)|$ in the established Erdős–Pósa result for $S$-rooted models of a fixed tree. The conjecture is stated in the more general setting of $(F,R)$-models and is open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Quentin Claus, Gwenaël Joret, Clément Rambaud and Eileen Robinson, “Erdős-Pósa property of rooted tree minors”, arXiv:2607.26638 (2026).
record.references:
